IMP-0095.title: Score and verdict decay: recompute when an input changes
IMP-0095.question_or_target: Implement freshness semantics so a stored quality score, vulnerability verdict, or conformance result carries the timestamp and input hashes it was computed from, and is marked STALE (and recomputed) when any input changes — because a green result computed last week against a live advisory database is not a control for today.
inputs: PINNED GROUND TRUTH: a green CI run DECAYS; gate-deps/osv-scanner queries a live advisory DB
IMP-0095.evidence_requirement: TWO independent signals: (1) changing one input hash flips the stored verdict to STALE; (2) an age-based sweep independently marks a verdict older than its freshness window as STALE even when no input hash changed — the advisory database is an input the registry cannot hash.
tests_required: tools/marketplace/tests/test_verdict_freshness.py::test_input_change_marks_stale
tools/marketplace/tests/test_verdict_freshness.py::test_age_alone_marks_stale
NEGATIVE CONTROL: a fresh verdict with unchanged inputs stays valid in the same run
IMP-0095.reviewer_requirement: Reviewer must confirm STALE is never rendered as PASS in any surface, including summary views.

IMP-0096.title: Benchmark evidence attachment with a reproducibility recipe
IMP-0096.question_or_target: Let a package version attach benchmark results, each carrying the harness version, the case set identifier, the environment fingerprint and a reproduction command — so a performance claim is an artifact someone else can re-run rather than a number in a description.

assigned_model_vendor_role.rationale: Deciding what makes a benchmark claim reproducible is the substance of the unit.

IMP-0096.evidence_requirement: TWO independent signals: (1) the attached record validates and contains every required reproducibility field; (2) the reproduction command is actually executed once in a clean environment and produces a result within the declared tolerance. A schema-valid record that cannot be re-run is not evidence.
tests_required: tools/marketplace/tests/test_benchmark_evidence.py::test_record_completeness
tools/marketplace/tests/test_benchmark_evidence.py::test_reproduction_command_runs
NEGATIVE CONTROL: a record with a missing environment fingerprint must be rejected
IMP-0096.reviewer_requirement: Reviewer must re-run one attached benchmark on different hardware and record the deviation.

IMP-0102.title: Deterministic lexical search index over the registry
IMP-0102.question_or_target: Build a BM25-style index over package name, description, tags and skill names with a total ordering that is stable across runs and independent of insertion order, and with no popularity term — ranking must be explainable from the query and the document alone.

assigned_model_vendor_role.rationale: Ranking determinism and index correctness are mechanically checkable.

IMP-0102.evidence_requirement: TWO independent signals: (1) the same query run 50 times returns one distinct result ordering; (2) the index rebuilt from a shuffled document order returns the identical ordering. Tie-breaking must be by a stable key, and the test must include an actual tie.
tests_required: tools/marketplace/tests/test_search_determinism.py::test_repeat_and_shuffle_invariance
tools/marketplace/tests/test_search_recall.py::test_known_package_is_findable_by_name_and_by_skill
NEGATIVE CONTROL: a query with no matches returns an explicit empty result, distinguishable from an index error
IMP-0102.reviewer_requirement: Reviewer must confirm the index covers the skills[] entries, not only top-level descriptions, since that is where the real corpus lives.

IMP-0107.title: Mirror conflict policy when upstream and mirror disagree
IMP-0107.question_or_target: Define and implement what happens when a mirror holds a different digest for the same package version than upstream: never silently prefer one, emit a conflict record naming both digests, and fail closed for installs of that version until resolved.

assigned_model_vendor_role.rationale: A digest disagreement is a potential supply-chain attack, not a merge problem.

IMP-0107.evidence_requirement: TWO independent signals: (1) a planted digest divergence produces a conflict record containing both digests and both sources; (2) an install of that version is refused, verified by a filesystem census showing nothing written. Recording without refusing is a half-implemented control.
tests_required: tools/marketplace/tests/test_mirror_conflict.py::test_divergence_recorded_and_install_refused
NEGATIVE CONTROL: matching digests install normally in the same run
the conflict must persist across restarts until explicitly resolved
IMP-0107.reviewer_requirement: Security reviewer must confirm there is no configuration that silently makes one side authoritative.
IMP-0107.retry_policy: no retry: a digest conflict is a security event requiring human resolution

IMP-0122.title: Rate-limit-aware registry client with jittered arrival staggering
IMP-0122.question_or_target: Implement the network client so a batch of installs staggers its arrivals, honours Retry-After, backs off exponentially with jitter, and surfaces a 429 storm as a named condition rather than as a cascade of individual failures — treating arrival rate as a scheduler input per the scaling doctrine.

assigned_model_vendor_role.rationale: Backoff behaviour is measurable against a fake server with an exact timing oracle.

IMP-0122.evidence_requirement: TWO independent signals: (1) against a fake server returning 429 with Retry-After, the observed inter-request intervals match the declared policy within tolerance; (2) the request arrival histogram for a 50-item batch shows staggering rather than a single burst, measured server-side. Client-side intent is not evidence of server-side arrival shape.
tests_required: tools/marketplace/tests/test_rate_limit_client.py::test_retry_after_is_honoured
tools/marketplace/tests/test_rate_limit_client.py::test_batch_arrivals_are_staggered
NEGATIVE CONTROL: a client without staggering must produce a burst histogram, proving the measurement discriminates
IMP-0122.reviewer_requirement: Reviewer must confirm jitter is genuinely random and not a fixed offset that re-synchronises the herd.
IMP-0122.retry_policy: the unit's own policy under test; implementation retries are bounded exponential with jitter, max 5, then a named 429-storm condition

IMP-0133.title: Add a typed workflow parameter model (Param, defaults, required, enum, secret-ref)
IMP-0133.question_or_target: Target: give Workflow a typed `params` surface so a blueprint is instantiable rather than hardcoded. Acceptance: a param declared `secret_ref` NEVER carries a literal value in the serialized workflow (it carries an env/secret-store reference), and the export path refuses to write a workflow whose params hold a value matching a credential-shaped pattern.
IMP-0133.evidence_requirement: Two signals: (1) a fixture with a literal token in a param fails export with a named violation; (2) an independent grep of the exported bytes for the fixture token returns zero hits.
tests_required: credential-shaped literal in a param must FAIL export; the secret_ref twin must PASS
mutation: weaken the pattern to match nothing and the leak test must go red
IMP-0133.reviewer_requirement: cross-vendor reviewer (Codex) plus one Claude adversarial reviewer - secret-adjacent surface
IMP-0133.retry_policy: two strikes then pivot - after the second failure on the same error fingerprint, enumerate >=2 alternative approaches before a third attempt (AGENTS.md 4b); a win-arg-limit failure retries once with --ignore-user-config and a prompt file, never inline argv
